transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-02 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Sara Malik (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Maya Lin (Hearthly Procurement), Trevor Sato (Hearthly Security), Priya Narayanan (Hearthly Platform)

Summary:
Quick commercial + legal intake to unblock procurement gate. Technical check on private vs hosted deployment, KMS requirements, egress costs and SLA commitment windows. Agreed to run scoped POC for latency & cost and exchange annotated contracts.

Topics: MSA redlines, DPA exceptions, SLA latency targets (p50/p95), Dedicated vs Hosted pricing buckets, KMS/HSM and key control, network egress, SOC2 scope, billing cadence.

[00:00] Sara: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we have about an hour. quick intros?
[00:12] Maya: Hey I'm Maya in procurement, I'll be owning the sourcing checklist and making sure we have the right commercial documents.
[00:18] Trevor: Trevor, security org, I'll be asking about keys, logs, and egress.
[00:22] Priya: Priya, platform, I'll share the traffic profile and help Diego run the POC.
[00:28] Diego: Diego from Redwood infra, happy to dig into topology and perf expectations.

[00:40] Sara: Cool. High level — Hearthly is looking for a vendor that can meet a production inference bar for customer-facing features, ideally with private network options. Procurement has questions about MSA/DPA timelines and pricing tiers, security wants KMS and audit logs. Is that accurate?
[00:58] Maya: Yes, exactly. We have a fiscal window so we need procurement sign-off before end of the month if possible. Also curious about usage tiers and any overage billing.
[01:10] Priya: On the technical side we use a mix of bursty traffic, p95 around 400ms target, p50 around 60-80ms. We'll want to test average token lengths, KV-cache usage, and whether dedicated pools can meet sustained throughput.

[01:35] Diego: Good — from Redwood side we support Hosted API (fast), Dedicated reserved capacity, and Private VPC/on-prem options. For latency targets, Dedicated usually gives most predictable p95. We also have prefix caching and batching knobs that help with cost.
[01:52] Trevor: On keys — we require customer-managed keys (BYOK) with HSM-backed KMS and audit trail for all inference requests. Does Redwood support that in Private?
[02:05] Diego: Yes, Private deployments support customer KMS integrations (we call out KMS/HSM in the DPA), but there are engineering steps: we need network peering and an HSM attestation plan. For Hosted, we can support envelope encryption but not full BYOK with HSM isolation today.
[02:23] Trevor: Hmm okay. That's a blocker for Hosted for us.
[02:28] Sara: Understood. Procurement note: I'll flag that as a security requirement. For MSA redlines, what are your top DPA asks?
[02:38] Maya: We need data residency commitments for EU customer records, deletion windows, and clarity on subprocessor lists. Also retention windows and ability to do audits.
[02:47] Trevor: Plus we need SOC2 Type II evidence and an option for enhanced logging retention (12 months).
[02:53] Diego: We can provide SOC2 reports; for retention we have tiered observability—longer retention is an add-on. Subprocessor list we can share and we have a standard DPA. Some of the DPA clauses around liability caps and breach notification timelines might need negotiation.
[03:11] Maya: Liability caps are usually negotiated at the commercial level; we'll want to surface if Redwood asks for full limitation.

[03:22] Priya: Quick technical question — how does Dedicated handle KV cache warmup for our workload? We have a lot of short chat sessions that hit the same prefixes.
[03:32] Diego: Our serving runtime has prefix/KV caching and continuous batching. For chat-like flows Dedicated with pinned model variants gives more cache locality; Hosted can do prefix caching but the eviction profile might be less deterministic. We'll instrument a POC to show effective hit rate.
[03:49] Priya: Great — we'll provide sample traces.

[04:00] Trevor: On network egress — do you bill egress separately? We have strict budgeting around cross-region egress and could be sensitive to per-GB fees.
[04:10] Sara: Egress fees are typically part of the commercial schedule; for Dedicated we can often include regional egress allowances in the commitment. For Hosted it's usually per-GB after free tier. We'll surface exact numbers in the quote.
[04:22] Maya: Can you give a rough ballpark now?
[04:25] Sara: Ballpark: Hosted multi-tenant egress is $0.08–0.12/GB, Dedicated committed plans can get to $0.02–0.06/GB depending on volume and region. We'll put exact numbers in a follow-up.
[04:38] Diego: Also worth noting quantization and batching profiles change token cost dramatically. We'll include example cost curves.

[04:50] Priya: Security — for audit logs we need traceability of per-request metadata, who called what, and the associated model version. Can Redwood provide token-level traces?
[05:03] Diego: We provide request-level metadata and changelogs in the Console. For Private deployments you can push logs to your SIEM via secure forwarding. For Hosted we have controlled exports and we can extend retention with add-ons.
[05:18] Trevor: Are there any known limitations with SAML SSO and RBAC? We need granular service-account scopes.
[05:25] Sara: We support SAML SSO and RBAC; however some fine-grained service-account RBAC is available in Private and Dedicated—Hosted has a slightly more opinionated RBAC model. We'll call out specifics in the security pack.
[05:40] Maya: Ok, on contracting — we'll need the MSA and DPA annotated. Any unusual standard clauses Redwood asks for?
[05:48] Sara: Standard MSA has indemnities, liability caps, and service levels. Usually negotiation centers on liability cap, breach notification, and audit rights in DPA. We'll send an annotated copy with suggested language.
[06:00] Priya: Is there an SLA for uptime and latency? Our SLAs are strict for latency-sensitive features.
[06:07] Diego: We have SLA tiers. Uptime SLAs are 99.9%+ for Dedicated and Private; latency SLAs are more nuanced — we provide latency SLOs and per-route dashboards, but strict p95 SLA commitments often map to Dedicated with a committed pool and burst buffer. We can engineer a canary rollout and fallback policies.
[06:29] Trevor: Do you include automatic fallback to a smaller model if the primary model misses latency? We need graceful degradation patterns.
[06:36] Diego: Yes, smart routing and automatic fallback to compatible model variants is a built-in pattern; we can configure per-route policies.

[06:46] Maya: Fiscal process — procurement needs cost transparency, committed spend, and exit terms. What is Redwood's minimum commitment for Dedicated?
[06:57] Sara: Typical Dedicated commitments start at mid-five figures per month, but we have flexible staged commitments for pilots. We'll prepare a model with a 3-step ramp: pilot (no long-term commit), pilot-to-dedicated option, and annual reserved capacity pricing.
[07:15] Priya: For the POC can we get short-term Dedicated-equivalent nodes so we can measure p95 under pinned cache?
[07:23] Diego: We can provide a short-term reserved pool for the POC under a pilot agreement; that will more closely mimic Dedicated behavior. We'll lock the model version and provide metrics.

[07:38] Trevor: Regarding subprocessor list and data residency, are there any EU-only deployments we can use for EU customers?
[07:46] Sara: Yes, we have region-specific Dedicated and Private options; for EU data residency we recommend Private VPC or dedicated EU pools. We'll include region mapping in the follow-up doc.

[07:58] Maya: One more on pricing: overage mechanics and invoice cadence. We need clear language on how overages are computed and the alerting thresholds.
[08:08] Sara: Overages are typically pro-rated on token/embedding usage in the month; we provide usage alerts and quotas. We can also do monthly or annual billing per customer preference. We'll surface exact invoice language for procurement review.

[08:24] Diego: I'll run the latency/cost POC using sample traces and a short reserved pool. I'll also capture cache hit rates and effective token cost with different batching parameters.
[08:34] Priya: We'll share traces and a test account with keys for the POC. Any restrictions on the sample data? We have PHI-like test vectors but redacted.
[08:44] Trevor: We need to confirm data handling for test data, telemetry, and logs. Can telemetry be disabled or scrubbed?
[08:50] Diego: We can scrub telemetry fields and in Private you can keep data in your VPC. For Hosted POC we'll use pseudonymized traces and agree on retention. We'll document that in the security pack.

[09:04] Sara: Ok let's surface the open items for legal: redlines on liability caps, breach notification timing, subprocessor list, and SOC2 attachments. I'll send annotated MSA/DPA.
[09:15] Maya: Great. Procurement will review that and come back with a contracting timeline.
[09:21] Trevor: Security will validate KMS attestation and logging approach once we get the security pack.
[09:27] Priya: Platform will hand over traces by EOD 2025-12-04.

[09:36] Diego: Anything else?
[09:39] Maya: Nothing from procurement. Thanks all.

Recap (last 3 minutes):
- Redwood to send annotated MSA + DPA and security pack (Sara)
- Redwood to run 48-hour POC on reserved pool and share latency/cost readouts (Diego)
- Hearthly to share traces, SOC2 scope, and egress table (Priya + Maya)
- Follow-up legal + infosec sync scheduled for 2025-12-15

Closing notes: conversation had typical transcription glitches, some product names turned into similar-sounding words (e.g., "KV cache" sometimes logged as "K V cash"), and timestamps roughly align with a 62-minute meeting.

End of transcript.
